formulas.title: Van der Waals Equation of State
formulas.description: Mean-field cubic equation of state for real fluids incorporating finite molecular excluded volume and attractive dispersion forces.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Modifies the ideal gas law $p v = R T$ by subtracting the molar excluded covolume $b$ from $v$ and adding an attractive internal pressure $a / v^2$ to $p$, predicting liquid-vapor condensation and a critical point.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Accounts for the two real-world facts ideal gases ignore: molecules take up space so they cannot overlap, and they pull weakly on each other when close.
formulas.interpretation: Provides the minimal analytical continuum model unifying gaseous, liquid, and supercritical fluid phases within a single cubic isotherm.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Mean-field thermodynamic closure of a hard-sphere fluid perturbed by spatially uniform long-range Kac attraction.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Reduces smoothly to the ideal gas law $p v = R T$ in the dilute high-temperature limit $v \gg b$ and $a / (v R T) \ll 1$; diverges as $v \to b^+$.

formulas.title: Van der Waals Molar Helmholtz Free Energy
formulas.description: Molar Helmholtz free energy of a van der Waals fluid derived from the canonical configurational partition function.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Evaluating $f = -R T \ln Z_N / N$ for hard-core excluded volume $v - b$ and mean-field attractive energy $-a/v$ yields $f_{\text{vdW}}(v, T)$, whose derivative $-(\partial f_{\text{vdW}} / \partial v)_T$ reproduces the van der Waals pressure.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Combines the entropic freedom of molecules moving inside the remaining free space $v - b$ with the energy lowered by their mutual attraction $-a/v$.
formulas.interpretation: Non-convexity of $f_{\text{vdW}}(v, T)$ below $T_c$ signals thermodynamic instability and motivates the common-tangent construction for phase separation.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Canonical ensemble free energy in the thermodynamic limit of a Kac potential with vanishing inverse range.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Strictly convex in $v$ for all $T \ge T_c$; develops a concave spinodal region for $T < T_c$ requiring convex-hull replacement.

semantic_variables.f_0(T): Purely temperature-dependent kinetic and internal free energy (J/mol)

formulas.title: Maxwell Equal-Area Construction
formulas.description: Thermodynamic integral condition determining the equilibrium saturation pressure and coexisting liquid and vapor volumes below the critical point.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Equating the chemical potentials $\mu(p_{\text{sat}}, T)$ of liquid ($v_l$) and vapor ($v_g$) forces the integral $\int_{v_l}^{v_g} [p(v, T) - p_{\text{sat}}(T)] \, dv = 0$, balancing the areas of the unphysical van der Waals loop above and below the isobar.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Draws a flat horizontal coexistence line across the S-shaped pressure loop so the lobe above the line and the lobe below have exactly equal area.
formulas.interpretation: Geometrically implements the convex-hull (common-tangent) envelope of the Helmholtz free energy, eliminating mechanically unstable negative-compressibility states.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Gibbs-Duhem chemical potential equality $\mu_l(T, p_{\text{sat}}) = \mu_g(T, p_{\text{sat}})$ across a first-order phase boundary.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Applies strictly for $0 < T < T_c$; as $T \to T_c^-$, both $v_l$ and $v_g$ converge continuously to $v_c$ and the coexistence interval vanishes.

formulas.title: Van der Waals Critical Compressibility Factor
formulas.description: Universal dimensionless ratio of critical pressure, molar volume, and thermal energy predicted by the van der Waals equation of state.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Substituting the critical inflection coordinates $T_c = 8a/(27Rb)$, $p_c = a/(27b^2)$, and $v_c = 3b$ cancels both $a$ and $b$ identically to give $Z_c = 3/8 = 0.375$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A pure number independent of molecular identity that measures how strongly a fluid deviates from ideal-gas behavior right at its critical point.
formulas.interpretation: Serves as a sharp quantitative benchmark: real noble gases measure $Z_c \approx 0.29$, quantifying the accuracy gap of simple cubic mean-field models.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Scale invariance of the two-parameter cubic inflection point $(\partial p/\partial v)_T = (\partial^2 p/\partial v^2)_T = 0$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Exact for the ideal van der Waals model ($0.375$); an ideal gas would have $Z = 1$ everywhere without a critical point.

formulas.title: Van der Waals Law of Corresponding States
formulas.description: Parameter-free dimensionless equation of state obtained by normalizing pressure, molar volume, and temperature by their critical values.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Introducing reduced variables $p_r = p/p_c$, $v_r = v/v_c$, and $T_r = T/T_c$ eliminates $a$, $b$, and $R$ completely from the van der Waals relation, placing all fluids onto a single universal thermodynamic surface.
formulas.intuitive_summary: When measured relative to their own critical points, vastly different gases like neon, argon, and methane obey the exact same pressure-volume-temperature map.
formulas.interpretation: Explains why simple nonpolar fluids sharing conformally similar pair potentials collapse onto a single empirical coexistence curve in reduced coordinates.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Dimensional rescaling invariance of any two-parameter intermolecular potential characterized by a single energy scale $\varepsilon$ and length scale $\sigma$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Critical point maps universally to $(p_r, v_r, T_r) = (1, 1, 1)$; breaks down quantitatively for quantum fluids (He, H_2) and strongly polar molecules.

formulas.title: Van der Waals Boyle Temperature
formulas.description: Characteristic temperature at which the second virial coefficient vanishes and attractive and repulsive non-ideal corrections cancel to leading order.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Expanding the van der Waals compressibility factor $Z = 1 + (b - a/(RT))/v + O(v^{-2})$ yields $B_2(T) = b - a/(RT)$, which crosses zero at $T_B = a/(Rb) = (27/8) T_c$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: The sweet-spot temperature where molecular attraction and molecular crowding balance out, making a real gas behave almost like an ideal gas over a broad pressure range.
formulas.interpretation: Separates low-temperature attraction-dominated compressibility ($Z < 1$ at low $p$) from high-temperature repulsion-dominated behavior ($Z > 1$).
formulas.symmetry_origin: Zero-crossing condition $B_2(T_B) = 0$ of the leading density correction in the virial expansion.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Predicts $T_B / T_c = 27/8 = 3.375$, compared with experimental ratios near $2.6$–$2.7$ for simple noble gases.

formulas.title: Joule-Thomson Throttling Coefficient
formulas.equation: \mu_{\text{JT}} = \left( \frac{\partial T}{\partial p} \right)_H = \frac{1}{C_p} \left[ T \left( \frac{\partial v}{\partial T} \right)_p - v \right]
formulas.description: Rate of temperature change with pressure during adiabatic isenthalpic throttling of a real gas through a valve or porous plug.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Applying the cyclic partial-derivative relation and Maxwell identity $(\partial s/\partial p)_T = -(\partial v/\partial T)_p$ at constant enthalpy $H = U + p V$ expresses $\mu_{\text{JT}}$ purely in terms of $C_p$ and thermal expansion.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Tells whether a pressurized gas cools down ($\mu_{\text{JT}} > 0$) or heats up ($\mu_{\text{JT}} < 0$) when forced through a narrow throttling valve.
formulas.interpretation: Governs cryogenic gas liquefaction: nitrogen cools at room temperature, whereas helium must be precooled below its inversion temperature near $40\text{ K}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Constant-enthalpy constraint $dH = T dS + V dp = 0$ combined with Maxwell thermodynamic reciprocity.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Vanishes identically for an ideal gas since $T (\partial v/\partial T)_p = v$; vanishes for real gases along the inversion curve where $T_{\text{inv,max}} = 2 a/(R b) = (27/4) T_c$ in van der Waals theory.

semantic_variables.H: Molar enthalpy held constant during throttling (J/mol)
